title: A green task gate stands for the fix leg, so the red-first proof runs once
description: Probe probe-8bf7e194: the proof ran a second time (~114 s per task) after a green task gate. Two causes in the record: the held gate run is a repeat (background gate read back), and gate_binding reads its copied row without following reusedFrom, so no background task gate can stand for the fix leg; and the joined sweep step keeps only a digest of its command, so it is spelled otherwise. Plus a bare sweep's per-file counts are cut at MAX_PATHS before the proof's file. Design: quality-gates-internal PLAN, probe-8bf7e194 and F933.
desiredOutcome: On a task whose green gate ran the proof's test file - as a repeated verdict, inside a joined step with the affected suites, or under the bare recorded sweep - the drive binds the fix leg to that run instead of running the proof's fix leg again, never where the helper's own fix leg would say red; and the gate's own record says which files its time went to.

findings.issue: A run that already bound through an EXACT step can now be refused because it also holds a BARE step. proof_steps now returns every step of the run in any of the three shapes, and gate_binding requires every one of them to stand. Here is a concrete case. The recorded spelling is `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --quiet {paths}`. The task gate declares both the proof's command (`... --quiet tests/test_mine.py`) and the bare `... --quiet`. Before this diff, the exact step stood on the files==1 shortcut and the run bound. Now the bare step is also a proof step. In quiet form it prints no per-file row, so _file_counts_standing refuses and the helper runs the fix leg again. The fault runs toward refusing, so it is not unsound, but it costs a run the drive used to save. A failed spelled_proof_paths also refuses the whole run, even when an exact step would stand alone.
findings.resolution: When at least one EXACT step stands, bind on it and do not require the joined or bare steps to stand too. Or read the joined and bare steps only when the run has no exact step. Add a case: a run with an exact step that stands plus a quiet bare step still binds.

tasks.title: A signal during the red-first proof's two legs leaves no run of the command alive
tasks.description: Case cl5 of tests/test_stamp_verification.py (SIGTERM mid-run tears down the process group of every leg) failed three times in a day on darwin: twice while two task gates ran at once, once (P174.2's re-gate on the phase tree) with nothing else running: 'pids [a, b], alive after the helper ended [b], 0.1s from the signal to its exit'. The helper exited within 0.1 s while one leg's process was still alive - a run of the user's command outliving the helper, which is the property cl5 guards. Find the race first by running the case in a loop (and under load) until it reproduces, and state which process survives (the task leg's on the main thread, or the baseline's on the worker thread) and why: e.g. a process spawned after the main thread's teardown snapshot, a Popen that returns after the stop but before started() is called, the main thread's own leg not torn down when the exception is raised outside _run_in's wait, or a teardown that signals the group before the child calls setsid. Fix the product if the race is there; fix the case only if the case is wrong, and say which. cl5 must stay a hard assertion. Also: the existing _TEARDOWN_BOUND / timing in this case are read by sk1 (clock-figure reasons) in the same suite.

add: tests/test_stamp_verification.py: a stop that lands while a leg is between spawning its process and registering it still tears that process down before the helper exits

outcome.technical: REPRODUCED: a scratch driver ran cl5's body (_signal_mid_run with SIGTERM) in a loop against one fixture repo. Before the fix: 2/200 idle; 7/200, 13/200 and 7/150 under 12 CPU burners on a 10-cpu darwin host. Every survivor was the TASK leg's process (its TMPDIR named task-tmp-), never the baseline's; helper exit 0.04-0.12 s after the signal. A scratch copy of the plugin, instrumented to dump the KeyboardInterrupt traceback, placed every hit inside the main thread's subprocess.Popen in _run_in: at _fork_exec's return, in the os.read of the exec pipe, in _close_pipe_fds, or on Popen's return before `proc` was bound. CAUSE: the task leg runs on the main thread; Python raises the signal's exception there between any two bytecodes, so one landing after the fork but before _run_in held the process skipped _run_in's teardown (Popen sat outside the try), and the main thread's own run is in no `live` list in _concurrent_legs. The process, in its own session (setsid), outlived the helper. The fault was in the product, not the case: cl5 stays the same hard assertion. FIX (stamp-verification.py): new _spawn_held starts the run from a thread of its own (no signal exception is raised there), into a holder dict, under a lock; _run_in now keeps the spawn, started(proc) and communicate in one try, and its BaseException arm takes the lock, sets cancelled and tears down whatever process the holder has, so the stop either cancels the start or waits for it and tears the run down. This covers every _run_in call (baseline, task, task-held, task-support, second, fix), not only the concurrent pair. The join poll became the constant JOIN_SLICE, shared with _concurrent_legs. Before the fix: FAIL il5 ... interrupt raised 'SIGTERM', returned None, processes made [37077], alive after `_run_in` raised [37077] (4/5). After the fix: PASS, alive [] (5/5). It adds no literal clock figure, so sk1 needs no row (passed in the gate). Skipped on Windows (no pthread_kill).
